title_en: An ETF for a Wild Oil Market
title_zh: 为狂野油市而生的 ETF：对话 Bloomberg Intelligence 的 Andre Yap
subtitle_zh: 解析主动型石油 ETF USE 的多空策略、展期成本与税务结构，看它能否成为 USO 的替代品。
description: An ETF for a Wild Oil Market

turns.en: Bloomberg Audio Studios. Podcasts. Radio. News.
turns.zh: Bloomberg Audio Studios。播客。电台。新闻。

turns.en: That's the thing that I find a little bit jarring. So when you hear absolute, you think of a positive number. You basically think of something going up. It's saying I'm giving you a return whether the markets are going up or down because of my ability to go long or short.
turns.zh: 这就是我觉着有点别扭的地方。你一听『绝对』（absolute），就会想到一个正数，基本上会想到某个东西在往上涨。它这名字是在说：不管市场是涨是跌，我都能给你一个回报，因为我有做多或做空的能力。

turns.en: Welcome to Giants. I'm Joel Weber.
turns.zh: 欢迎收听 Trillions。我是 Joel Weber。

turns.en: And I'm Eric Balchunas.
turns.zh: 我是 Eric Balchunas。

turns.en: It's hard not to talk about oil this year. It's just been a theme. But I was surprised for this episode to learn about an ETF other than the United States Oil Fund, USO, which is just the big dog in oil. And it's the one that we usually talk about when we talk about oil. But this other ETF is pretty dynamic, same flows. And it has some aspects that normal investors might want to know about. And I can say this for the first time ever, you could actually like maybe think about being a retail investor who touches oil. It still holds futures, which is just the nature of a commodity ETF. But you won't get a surprise from tax season either. This time on Trillions, a new oil trade. Every time we talk about oil, we talk about a certain ETF, which is the United States Oil Fund. The ticker for that is USO. And your research has surfaced a new one. Which is it?
turns.zh: 今年你很难不聊石油，它就是个绕不开的主题。但为了做这一期，让我吃惊的是，我了解到除了 United States Oil Fund（USO）之外还有一只 ETF——USO 可是石油界的大佬，也是我们一聊石油通常会提到的那只。但这另一只 ETF 相当灵活，资金流也一样。它有一些普通投资者可能想了解的方面。而且我可以这么说，这是头一回，你或许真的可以考虑当一个碰石油的散户投资者。它仍然持有期货（futures），这是商品型 ETF 的天性使然。但报税季你也不会被吓一跳。本期 Trillions，一个新的石油交易。每次我们聊石油，都会提到某只 ETF，也就是 United States Oil Fund，代码是 USO。而你们的研究又挖出了一只新的。是哪只？

turns.en: Yeah, right. So USO is the famous one. It holds futures very close to what we call front month. So it's very sensitive, but has some other issues which we'll discuss. But it's by far the most popular. But there's another one that is just maybe a little more risk averse and a little safer for people than USO called USE, which is U-S-E. which is the word for I want to use something, or the plural word for you in Philly, use guys. Sorry, bad joke. Local joke. It's true, though. I hear use once a week here. Anyway, the USCF Energy Commodity Strategy Absolute Return Fund. So we'll go in what it is. But just real quick, Joel, I find this oil trade fascinating because it just seems like Trump is caught in between these two opposing forces. And that's why this oil trade has been so fun for traders because Iran does something to irk him and he goes wild with the tough talk. And then oil spikes because like, oh, they're going to close the straits. Then stocks go down because oil spiking and inflation fears ramp up. And he's like, oh, no, because he loves the stock market being up. So he's like, oh, we have a deal or we may have a deal.
turns.zh: 对，没错。USO 是那只大名鼎鼎的。它持有的期货非常接近我们说的近月（front month），所以它非常敏感，但也有一些别的问题，我们待会儿聊。不过它绝对是最受欢迎的。但还有另一只，也许比 USO 更厌恶风险一点、对普通人更安全一点，叫 USE，拼作 U-S-E，正好是『我想用某个东西』那个词，或者在费城是『你们』的复数说法，use guys。抱歉，冷笑话，本地梗。不过是真的，我在这儿每周都能听到 use 这个词。总之，它叫 USCF Energy Commodity Strategy Absolute Return Fund。我们待会儿细说它是什么。但先说一句，Joel，我觉得这个石油交易特别有意思，因为 Trump 看起来就是被夹在两股相反的力量中间。这也是为什么这个石油交易对交易者来说这么好玩：Iran 做点什么事惹恼他，他就疯狂放狠话；然后油价飙升，因为大家想『哦，他们要封锁海峡了』；接着股市下跌，因为油价飙升、通胀担忧升温；然后他就慌了，因为他喜欢股市上涨，于是他又说『哦，我们达成协议了，或者可能要达成协议了』。

turns.en: Yeah, I've heard that a few times.
turns.zh: 对，这话我听过好几回了。

turns.en: And there's probably been like, I'm going to no lie. 20 stock market rallies based on hopes of a deal. It's like that Dave Chappelle meme, got any more hopes of a deal? Anyway, and once the stock market goes back up, he goes back to being upset about Iran and around and around we go. So we thought we'd focus on the oil side of this equation. And Andre picked a real hidden gem here.
turns.zh: 而且不夸张地说，可能已经有 20 次股市上涨是靠『达成协议的希望』撑起来的。就像 Dave Chappelle 那个表情包：『还有没有别的达成协议的希望了？』总之，一旦股市重新涨上去，他就又开始对 Iran 恼火，然后我们就这么一圈一圈地转。所以我们想聚焦在这个等式的石油这一侧。而 Andre 挑中了一个真正的沧海遗珠。

turns.en: And Andre is Andre Yap. He's a ETF investor. Research Senior Associate at Bloomberg Intelligence. Andre, welcome back to Trillions.
turns.zh: Andre 就是 Andre Yap，是 Bloomberg Intelligence 的 ETF 投资研究高级专员（Senior Associate）。Andre，欢迎再次回到 Trillions。

turns.en: Thank you for having me.
turns.zh: 谢谢你们邀请我。

turns.en: Okay, now remind our listeners how the ETF of the moment happens. You guys are constantly looking at ETFs, but this is a little different in that you have some screening mechanisms to see what's got some momentum.
turns.zh: 好，现在给我们的听众再讲讲『当下热门 ETF』（ETF of the moment）是怎么选出来的。你们一直在盯各种 ETF，但这个有点不一样，因为你们有一些筛选机制，来看哪些有势头。

turns.en: Yeah, so we take a quantitative approach to try to identify ETFs which are having a moment. Basically, we screen based on two criteria. We screen based on returns. The returns need to be positive, particularly over the short term to show that there's some momentum happening right now. And we also look to see an increase in trading volume. So we want to see typically at least a 50% jump in the number of shares that are being traded. for us to even consider it as a candidate for the ETF of the moment.
turns.zh: 对，我们用一套量化方法来识别那些正当红的 ETF。基本上，我们按两个标准来筛。一是看回报，回报必须为正，尤其是短期回报，以此表明眼下确实有势头。二是看成交量是否放大，所以我们通常希望看到成交股数至少跳增 50%，才会把它当成『当下热门 ETF』的候选。

turns.en: And if all of those signals kind of work in its favor, what distinguishes an ETF of the moment?
turns.zh: 如果这些信号都对它有利，那么是什么让一只 ETF 脱颖而出、成为『当下热门』呢？

turns.en: I think what distinguishes it, why we would probably pick amongst the peer group, is something that is topical, something that people want to hear about, something that we want to explore, and that seems interesting or fun or just weird.
turns.zh: 我觉得让它脱颖而出的、也是我们会从同类里挑中它的原因，是它得应景、是大家都想听的话题、是我们想去深挖的东西，而且看起来有意思、好玩，或者干脆就是够怪。

turns.en: And usually... Because it's of the moment, it's like we're getting a little sneak peek of something that's going to be trending in the near future. So talk to us about USE, is the ticker, the USCF Energy Commodity Strategy Absolute Return Fund. That's a pretty long mouthful of a name. What does it do and how does it work?
turns.zh: 而且通常……因为它是『当下热门』，就像让我们提前偷看到某个在不久的将来会火起来的东西。那来跟我们聊聊 USE 吧，这是它的代码，全称 USCF Energy Commodity Strategy Absolute Return Fund。这名字可真够拗口的。它是做什么的，又是怎么运作的？

turns.en: Yeah, it's an absolute mouthful. So it's an actively managed ETF. that utilizes long, short, or spread positions in futures contracts tied with energy commodities. By energy commodities, I don't mean simply crude. So it's tied to WTI and Brent crude, as well as natural gas, gasoline, diesel, and I think gas oil. So it spans the energy gamut. So that's how it differs a little bit from USO, the more popular brother.
turns.zh: 对，名字是真拗口。它是一只主动管理型 ETF（actively managed ETF），在跟能源商品挂钩的期货合约上做多、做空或做价差（spread）头寸。说到能源商品，我指的不仅仅是原油。它挂钩 WTI 和 Brent 原油，还有天然气、汽油、柴油，我记得还有瓦斯油（gas oil），所以它覆盖了整个能源谱系。这也是它跟那位更出名的『老大哥』USO 有点不一样的地方。

turns.en: Okay. And speaking of which, we've talked about USO a lot. The thing that Eric always talks about with USO, the United States Oil Fund, we're rolling futures with that ETF, which instantly puts it in a world where retail investors in particular are potentially going to get punished. Does this still touch futures? And if so, how does the role differ from what USO does?
turns.zh: 好。说到这个，我们聊过 USO 很多次了。Eric 老是讲的那点——USO，也就是 United States Oil Fund，它要展期期货（rolling futures），这一下就把它放进一个尤其是散户可能要吃亏的世界。这只新的还碰期货吗？如果碰，它的展期跟 USO 的做法有什么不同？

turns.en: Yeah, it still touches futures. So it's still buyer beware somewhat. It differs in that with USO, it basically only goes long. So you can get into a situation where you're basically facing the rolled yield, where you can basically get positive or negative returns, depending on whether the market's in contango or backwardation. The same risk exists with use. However, the strategy is more dynamic because it has the capacity to go long, to go short, as well as take spread positions. So it's a little bit more dynamic in its strategy and implementation of it. than USO, in my opinion.
turns.zh: 对，它还是碰期货，所以在一定程度上仍是『买家自行小心』。区别在于，USO 基本上只做多，所以你会陷入一种境地：直接面对展期收益（roll yield），可能拿到正回报也可能拿到负回报，取决于市场是期货溢价（contango）还是现货溢价（backwardation）。USE 也存在同样的风险。不过它的策略更灵活，因为它既能做多、也能做空，还能做价差头寸。所以在我看来，它在策略及其执行上比 USO 更灵活一些。

turns.en: Why is that interesting, Eric?
turns.zh: 为什么这一点有意思呢，Eric？

turns.en: Yeah, because, I mean, just for anybody out there, think about the oil futures curve and words like contango. And that curve changes a lot based on what people think oil will be worth in the future. And it's a very specific local market that experts trade in. But if you're not one of those people, this is sort of like saying, hey, look, let's take this company that knows this market well and let them kind of trade around this and try to exploit the oil situation as best they can and really free them up to go short if they need to. And by doing long short, you also bring your volatility down a little, right? Because sometimes you have some offsetting positions. So this is a slightly less volatile ETF than USO. So in the downturns, when Trump was like, told everybody there's hopes of a deal and oil came crashing down, this one will come down a little less. But pound for pound, I just think it's an interesting option. It's still very small. The price is still at 79 basis points. It only has 7 million. So there are some things that I don't love about it. But I think there are just some areas of the market where handing it over to an active manager who can just do things with no restraints can work well, potentially, again. So this is just an alternative to USO, which is much more of a, robotic ETF that's just giving you the front month futures for better or worse.
turns.zh: 对，因为，我是说，对在场的任何人来说，想想石油期货曲线，还有像 contango 这样的词。这条曲线会根据大家认为未来石油值多少钱而大幅变化，而且那是一个由专家交易的、非常专门的小众市场。但如果你不是那类人，这就有点像在说：嘿，看，我们把这家深谙此道的公司请来做，让他们围绕这个市场去交易，尽他们所能去利用石油行情，并且真正放开手脚，需要时就能做空。而且通过做多又做空，你还能把波动率压低一点，对吧？因为有时候你会有一些相互对冲的头寸。所以这是一只波动比 USO 略小的 ETF。在下行行情里，当 Trump 告诉大家『有达成协议的希望』、油价应声暴跌时，这只跌得会少一点。但总体权衡下来，我就是觉得它是个有意思的选择。它规模仍然很小，费率还是 79 个基点（basis points），资产只有 700 万美元。所以有些方面我并不喜欢。但我觉得市场里就是有那么一些领域，把它交给一个能不受约束地操作的主动管理人，可能效果会很好——再说一次。所以这只是 USO 的一个替代品，而 USO 更像是一只机械化的 ETF，不管好坏，它就是给你近月期货。

turns.en: So you actually have a human in the cockpit with this. Andre, what's the performance been like?
turns.zh: 所以这只其实是有一个真人在驾驶舱里操作的。Andre，它的业绩表现怎么样？

turns.en: Well, it's been somewhat of a mixed bag, but this year the performance has been pretty good. So if you're looking at it on a year-to-date basis, it's up 83%. But if you compare it to USO or just the WTI in general, WTI crude, those are up 100% 86% for USO and 153% year to date for WTI. So it does lag them a little bit. But if you look at it just over the third quarter, which is basically from July till right now, we're not completely through. It's pretty much in line. They're all up about 35%.
turns.zh: 嗯，可以说是好坏参半，但今年它的表现相当不错。如果按年初至今（year-to-date）来看，它涨了 83%。但如果拿它跟 USO、或者整体上的 WTI 原油比，它们涨了 100%……USO 年初至今是 86%，WTI 是 153%，所以它确实稍微落后它们一点。不过如果只看第三季度，也就是基本上从 7 月到现在——我们还没完全走完——它基本是同步的，三者都涨了大约 35%。

turns.en: Yeah, I mean, 50% return year to date is still pretty good. Although USO is up 100%. But this is, by the way, I just got to say one thing, USO, The people trading this thing have done a good job of taking profits. So there's been a lot of flows in and out of USO, and people generally think it just loses money for people, but it's actually been traded pretty effectively. When it goes up, people pull the money out, and then when it goes down, they put it in. I think the trading crowd is really on to this sort of like– what would you call it? Loop or cycle that Trump is involved in with getting mad at Iran and then like trying to do a deal, and it's becoming pretty profitable trade.
turns.zh: 对，我是说，年初至今 50% 的回报还是挺不错的，尽管 USO 涨了 100%。不过顺便说一句，我得讲一件事：USO，交易它的那帮人获利了结做得很好。所以 USO 有大量资金进进出出，大家一般觉得它只会让人亏钱，但实际上它被交易得相当有效。它涨的时候，大家把钱抽出来；跌的时候，再把钱投进去。我觉得交易圈是真摸透了 Trump 卷入的这种——你该怎么叫它呢？——循环或周期：对 Iran 发火，然后又想去达成协议。而这正在变成一笔相当赚钱的交易。

turns.en: Back to to use for a second use what does absolute return mean since that's actually part of the name right.
turns.zh: 我们回到 USE 一下。USE 里的『绝对回报』（absolute return）是什么意思？因为这毕竟是它名字的一部分，对吧。

turns.en: That's the thing that i find a little bit jarring so when you hear absolute you think of a positive number you don't think of or you basically think of something going up um and i think what it implies or at least what i got from the name when it says absolute return it's saying i'm giving you a return whether the markets are going up or down because of my ability to go long or short and that's an implication but if you read through the actual prospect it doesn't make any claims to say that it actually does that where it's saying we'll generate positive return no matter what happens with the market so it's a little bit of a catch-all and what's funny So we did some analysis of users historical returns, and we basically tried to see how well they're tracking the market to generate positive returns, regardless of what the market is doing. In order to do that, we categorize the market into up regimes or down regimes. Up regimes being essentially periods where the 50 day moving average is above the benchmark. And that has been positive for at least the past five days. So we're not looking for spikes to somewhat deter or the dictates it is. We're looking for a smooth transition and down markets being essentially the opposite. And what we found is essentially uses return is just positive correlated regardless of the market regime. So when markets are up, use, it delivers positive return. When markets are down, it delivers the same returns. It delivers negative returns. So it moves in line with the market, which is to say it is positively correlated. So the absolute return might be a little bit of a stretch.
turns.zh: 这就是我觉着有点别扭的地方。你一听『绝对』，就会想到一个正数，基本上会想到某个东西在往上涨。我觉得它暗示的、至少我从『绝对回报』这个名字里读到的意思是：不管市场是涨是跌，我都能给你一个回报，因为我有做多或做空的能力。这是一种暗示，但如果你通读实际的招募说明书（prospectus），它并没有做任何这样的承诺，也就是说它没说『无论市场怎样，我们都会创造正回报』。所以这名字有点像是个万能标签。有意思的是，我们对 USE 的历史回报做了一些分析，基本上是想看看，无论市场怎么走，它跟踪市场、创造正回报的能力到底如何。为此，我们把市场划分为上行区间（up regimes）和下行区间（down regimes）。上行区间基本上是指 50 日均线在基准之上、并且过去至少五天持续为正的那些时段——所以我们不是在看某种短暂的尖峰，我们要的是平滑的过渡；下行市场则基本相反。我们发现，本质上 USE 的回报就是正相关的，不管市场处于哪种区间。也就是说，市场上涨时，USE 交付正回报；市场下跌时，它交付的还是那样的回报——它交付的是负回报。所以它是跟着市场同步走的，换句话说就是正相关。因此『绝对回报』这个说法可能有点言过其实。

turns.en: Yeah, I agree.
turns.zh: 对，我同意。

turns.en: I think when you see absolute return, I kind of think hedge fundish. It's not tracking a benchmark, you know, like a regular active mutual fund will be like benchmark to the S & P. That's not absolute return. That's trying to get return over the benchmark. This is just saying, hey, we can kind of try to get return in any environment. But to Andre's point, that is one ding on this fund is that you would think I would like to see more buffer in the downturn. I would like to see it go short a little more. when the market's going down, and like you said, overall volatility coming down and be a little more like a hedge fund. But to Andre's point, it just seems like it has a lot of beta to oil, more than you would expect with the name absolute return. And that's an important point here. But again, it is the active manager's choice. Maybe they are just thinking that's what you need to do at this time. But we'll see. It's also just good to highlight that when you go into an ETF category, and there's the famous one, like USO is probably like you know, the majority lion's share of the assets. There are, you know, multiple choices of ways to do this. There's another one called UNL that holds all of the months at once. And that's just like owning the whole curve. And that would be also another option for somebody who wants a sort of kinder, gentler oil play. They're all red light products because oil futures is a really exotic, wild category. And the way they roll can cause unhidden costs and Yeah, just be very careful. This is very like a lot of trap doors and snares. That's the case for active, but still, even with that knowledge, it's hard.
turns.zh: 我觉得你一看到『绝对回报』，我就会往对冲基金那个方向想。它不跟踪某个基准，你知道，就像一只普通的主动型共同基金会以 S&P 为基准，那不是绝对回报，那是想在基准之上多赚回报。而『绝对回报』是在说：嘿，我们基本上能在任何环境下都设法赚到回报。但就像 Andre 说的，这也是这只基金的一个减分项：你会以为——我本来希望在下行时看到更多缓冲，希望它在市场下跌时多做空一点，就像你说的，整体波动率降下来，更像一只对冲基金。但按 Andre 的说法，它似乎对石油有很大的贝塔（beta），比『绝对回报』这个名字给你的预期要大，而这是个重要的点。不过话说回来，这是主动管理人的选择，也许他们就是觉得当下需要这么做。我们走着瞧。还有一点也值得强调：当你进入一个 ETF 类别，里面有那只大名鼎鼎的——比如 USO 大概占了绝大部分、狮子大口的资产份额——其实做这件事有多种选择。还有另一只叫 UNL，它一次性持有所有月份的合约，那就相当于拥有了整条曲线。对于想要一种更温和、更温柔的石油玩法的人来说，这也是另一个选项。它们全都是『红灯』（red light）产品，因为石油期货真的是一个非常奇特、狂野的类别，而它们的展期方式会造成隐藏成本。所以，一定要非常小心，这里面有很多活板门和陷阱。主动型的就是这样，但即便如此，有了这些认知，它依然很难。

turns.en: So that red light mention is actually a Bloomberg Intelligence classification system, and it's not really meant to be a judgment. It's just if you're going to use these products, red light means there's going to be some technical aspects of the products that you should know about.
turns.zh: 所以刚才提到的『红灯』其实是 Bloomberg Intelligence 的一套分类系统，它并不是真要下个评判。它的意思只是：如果你要用这些产品，『红灯』代表这些产品会有一些你应当了解的技术性方面。

turns.en: Yeah, anything that rolls futures, whether it's VIX futures or natural gas or oil is an instant red light because it's just so on. It's an unusual thing. Normal people don't really think about it or know about it. Like if I said the word contango to any of my friends or family, they would think I'm talking about a dance. Yeah. But contango is when you roll futures and everyone's more expensive. So you pay a little, let me give one quick thing here. This is, this helps people crystallize why futures are so brutal. Put it this way. When futures are expiring, they're going to send oil to your house. And like nobody in their right mind wants oil sent to their house because it's toxic and you can't store it in your backyard. So the more cumbersome the commodity is to store, like oil or corn, the more the market knows that and it's going to price up the next month. So for you, you want to get out before it expires and you have to pay up. So in other words, the storage cost and pain in the assness is baked into the curve because they know you don't want to take delivery. So just think of how annoying the commodity is. And that's how much you're probably going to pay in these roll costs. So that's why gold isn't that bad. Like the futures market's pretty chill because you could get gold delivered to your house. It's no big deal. But oil, corn, I mean, you know, I guess coffee would be OK. i guess the more the delivery is no big deal the less the curve will hurt you but oil is like the worst you know nobody wants a barrel of oil sent to their house.
turns.zh: 对，任何要展期期货的东西——不管是 VIX 期货、天然气还是石油——都是即刻的『红灯』，因为这实在太……这是件不寻常的事，普通人根本不会去想它、也不了解它。比如我要是跟我任何一个朋友或家人说出 contango 这个词，他们会以为我在说某种舞蹈。是的，但 contango 是指你展期期货时、每一个月都更贵，所以你要多付一点。让我在这儿快速讲一件事，这能帮大家想清楚期货为什么如此残酷。这么说吧：当期货到期时，他们要把石油送到你家。而没有哪个神志正常的人想让石油被送到家里，因为它有毒，你也没法把它存在后院。所以一种商品越是难储存——比如石油或玉米——市场就越清楚这一点，就会把下一个月的价格抬高。于是对你来说，你想在到期之前脱身，可你就得付钱。换句话说，储存成本和那种『烦人劲儿』已经被计入了曲线里，因为他们知道你不想接收实物交割。所以你就想想这种商品有多招人烦，那大概就是你在这些展期成本上要付的钱。这也是为什么黄金没那么糟——黄金的期货市场相当轻松，因为你可以让人把黄金送到你家，没什么大不了的。但石油、玉米……我是说，你懂的，我猜咖啡还行。我猜交割越是无所谓，曲线对你的伤害就越小；但石油是最糟的，你知道，没人想让一桶石油被送到自己家。

turns.en: It's a great way to think about it that i don't think you've ever said it that way before that totally makes sense and i actually i don't want coffee sent to me because it'd be like a raw commodity it's not like it's been roasted or anything it'd just be like beans i don't need that uh So we've talked a little bit about the potential downsides of use and also just the space. One thing that we haven't talked about is the tax side. And this ETF use is structured a little differently than USO. And I just want to take a moment to talk about that because it is, Andre, an open-ended investment company. What does that mean? And what does that have to do with taxes?
turns.zh: 这是个很棒的思考角度，我觉得你以前从没这么讲过，这完全说得通。而且说实话，我也不想让人把咖啡送到我家，因为那会是一种原始商品，又不是烘焙过的什么的，就只是一堆豆子，我用不着那个。呃，所以我们已经聊了一点 USE 潜在的下行风险，也聊了这个领域本身。有一件事我们还没谈，就是税务这一侧。而 USE 这只 ETF 的结构跟 USO 有点不一样。我想花点时间谈谈这个，因为——Andre——它是一家开放式投资公司（open-ended investment company）。这是什么意思？这跟税又有什么关系？

turns.en: Let's just try to simplify it and forget the terminology. Essentially, when you're invested in something like USO, you could get an unexpected tax bill regardless of whether you have sold the ETF. So based on the structure of that actual, the way it's organized and structured, whatever happens on the fund level could affect you as an investor because in reality, you are a partner. Now with you, the difference is it's structured more like your everyday ETF. your tax bill is contingent upon your activity with the fund. Whether you buy or sell it or make a profit or a loss, that is what will drive your tax liability or your tax position. So that's the upside of an ETF like this in the way that it's structured compared to an older ETF like use.
turns.zh: 我们尽量把它简化，抛开那些术语。本质上，当你投资像 USO 这样的东西时，不管你有没有卖出这只 ETF，你都可能收到一笔意想不到的税单。因为基于它实际的组织和结构方式，基金层面发生的任何事都可能影响到你这个投资者——因为在现实中，你是一名合伙人（partner）。而 USE 的不同之处在于，它的结构更像你日常见到的那种 ETF：你的税单取决于你在这只基金上的操作，无论你是买入还是卖出、是赚还是亏，那才是驱动你的纳税义务或税务状况的东西。所以这就是这样一只 ETF 在结构上、相比像 USO 那种更老式的 ETF 的优势所在。

turns.en: The other problem with these commodity future ETFs generally, although some have solved this, is in USO, for example, the form, the tax form you get is called a K-1 and it comes like at a different time. And I've never filled one out, but I remember interviewing people for my first book about it. And one lady said, look, it's not the end of the world, but it sucks. It's like a paper cut. You know, it's just annoying as hell. And nobody likes that. So there's actually some commodity ETFs that use a structure where they can avoid the K-1 and they put no K-1 in the name. That's how brutal that tax form is, especially for advisors. And this does not have a K1. Use doesn't, USO does. And not having a K1 is a nice feature, but it's also not the end of the world. I mean, some people go, when it comes to taxes and tax forms, I think there's just such a crazy reaction and fear of all that stuff. But anyway, good to just get all that information out. It's just another reason the commodity futures area is a rated R or red light because it's just so much to untangle here.
turns.zh: 这类商品期货 ETF 普遍存在的另一个问题——尽管有些已经解决了——比如说 USO，你拿到的那张税表叫 K-1，而且它来的时间还跟别的不一样。我自己从没填过，但我记得为我的第一本书采访别人时聊过这个。有位女士说：『看，这不是世界末日，但真的很糟糕，就像被纸划了个口子，烦死人了。』没人喜欢那样。所以其实有一些商品 ETF 采用了一种能避开 K-1 的结构，还会把『no K-1』直接写进名字里。这张税表就是这么折磨人，尤其是对投资顾问而言。而这只是没有 K-1 的：USE 没有，USO 有。没有 K-1 是个不错的特点，但也不是什么天大的事。我是说，有些人一谈到税和税表，就会有种夸张的反应和恐惧。总之，把这些信息都说出来是好事。这也只是商品期货领域被评为『限制级』（rated R）或『红灯』的又一个原因，因为这里要理清的东西实在太多了。

turns.en: Yeah, definitely buy everywhere.
turns.zh: 对，绝对的。
